paper_title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
core_problem: Building generally capable embodied agents that continuously explore, plan, and develop new skills in open-ended worlds. Classical RL and imitation learning operate on primitive actions, which is challenging for systematic exploration, interpretability, and generalization. Recent LLM-based agents harness world knowledge to generate action plans but are not lifelong learners that can progressively acquire, update, accumulate, and transfer knowledge over extended time spans. LLMs also struggle to produce correct action code consistently in one shot.
methodology_summary: VOYAGER is an LLM-powered embodied lifelong learning agent in Minecraft that continuously explores, acquires diverse skills, and makes novel discoveries without human intervention. It has three components: an automatic curriculum that maximizes exploration, an ever-growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving complex behaviors, and an iterative prompting mechanism that incorporates environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification for program improvement. It interacts with GPT-4 via blackbox queries without fine-tuning. Skills are temporally extended, interpretable, and compositional.
datasets_eval: Evaluated in MineDojo, an open-source Minecraft AI framework. Baselines include ReAct, Reflexion, and AutoGPT re-interpreted for MineDojo. Evaluation metrics cover exploration performance, tech tree mastery, map coverage, and zero-shot generalization to novel tasks in a new world.
empirical_results: VOYAGER demonstrates strong in-context lifelong learning. It obtains 3.3x more unique items, travels 2.3x longer distances, and unlocks key tech tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA. It builds an ever-growing reusable, interpretable, generalizable skill library and can utilize it in a new Minecraft world to solve novel tasks from scratch, while other methods struggle to generalize.
explicit_limitations: LLMs struggle to produce correct action code consistently in one shot, requiring iterative refinement with environment feedback and error traces. Classical RL/imitation approaches operating on primitive actions face challenges in systematic exploration, interpretability, and generalization. Existing LLM agents are not lifelong learners capable of progressive acquisition, update, accumulation, and transfer of knowledge over extended time spans.
